fix.notes: Pure UI change in one JSX file, matching existing code style and class naming conventions. The ⇤/⇥ Unicode arrows are the same style as the existing ←/→. No Python, CSS, or test files needed changing.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The pagination controls in `shared_web/static/js/table.jsx` only showed the item range (e.g. "1-20 of 150") and prev/next arrows. There was no indication of current page number out of total pages, and no way to jump directly to the first or last page.

## What changed

In `renderPagination()` in `table.jsx`:
- Computed `numPages = Math.ceil(total / this.state.pageSize)` and `currentPage = this.state.page + 1`
- Added a `Page N of M` display in a new `page-number section` span
- Added a ⇤ (first-page) link before the ← arrow, active when `page > 0`, calling `this.movePage(0)`
- Added a ⇥ (last-page) link after the → arrow, active when `end < total`, calling `this.movePage(numPages - 1)`
- Inactive states use the existing `inactive` class pattern for visual consistency

## Validation

`uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed. This is a JSX-only UI change; the Python unit suite has no tests covering this component and no DB was configured in this environment. The change is confined to 13 inserted lines in one file.

Fixes #6657
